given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans are lent on 2026-03-02, so they are due 2026-03-16, and the clock is then set to 2026-03-17 before the job runs.
The clock is always at 10:00Z, far from midnight, so a version that worked out today in local time would still pass in nearly every timezone.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The database is new in memory and the job runs once, so neither loan has a reminder when it runs.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: The fake's `sent` list must hold exactly the two reminders, each with its own memberId, loanId and dueOn, so skipping the call or sending the wrong member fails.
The reminders table must hold one row for each loan, and line 43 also pins the row count at 2.
`sent_on` must be 2026-03-17, today's date, not the dueOn of 2026-03-16.
B3's test fails if a refused reminder is recorded, and that is the only way recording before asking would show.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so on the second run loan1 already has today's reminder.
loan2 is overdue and is returned before the job runs.
The third loan is lent on 03-03, so it is due 03-17, which is today: the exact edge case.

then.why: `toMatchObject` on an array also checks its length, so `sent` must be exactly one reminder, for loan1, which rules out a second loan1 send and any send for loan2 or loan3.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with the reason 'Notifications API answered 503'.

The fake only has a 'refused' result, and no test at any level drops the connection. B5's client test has no unreachable case, so nothing shows that a failed connection reaches the job as a refusal rather than an exception.

then.why: The reminders table must equal exactly [loan2 on 2026-03-17].
The log entry must match exactly, including level 'warn' and event 'reminder.failed'.
The fields must equal { loanId: loan1, error: 'Notifications API answered 503' }, which is the fake's refusal reason.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: The refused loan1 is due earlier than loan2, so it is handled first, and loan2 must still be sent and recorded.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans, one of them refused, go through one full run.

then.why: The last log entry must have event 'reminders.finished'.
The level must be exactly 'info'.
The fields must equal { sent: 2, failed: 1 }, so dropping either count fails.

given.why: Every B5 test calls the real client with a fixed reminder.

then.why: The recorded request method must be 'POST'.
The path must be '/notifications', and the handler only matches the NOTIFY_URL host; unhandled requests are errors (tests/support/http-interceptor.setup.ts:4), so a wrong host or path fails.
The content-type must be exactly 'application/json', and the body is parsed as JSON.
The body is compared with `toEqual`, so renaming any key or changing the template value fails.
Separate tests answer 200, 202 and 204 and each expect 'accepted', so a version that accepts only 200 fails.
Only a 400 is tried. A client that refused only 4xx and accepted 5xx would pass, though 5xx is the most likely answer when the API refuses.

then.part: or a failed connection as refused
then.why: No test makes the connection fail (for example with `HttpResponse.error()`), so a client that throws instead of refusing would pass.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain '400', so a generic reason fails.

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: No case covers an unreachable API, so the reason it gives is never checked.
